title: Mapping-space detection of small generated saturation
statement: Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category and $S$ a small set of its arrows. Say that $Z$ is $S$-local if $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C_S$ be the left adjoint to the full inclusion of these local objects (which exists by [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints]). For an arrow $f:A\to B$, the following conditions are equivalent: $Lf$ is an equivalence; $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $S$-local $Z$; and $f$ belongs to the smallest class $\langle S\rangle$ containing $S$ and all equivalences and closed under two-out-of-three, retracts, pushouts and small colimits in the arrow infinity category. Every unit $A\to LA$ belongs to $\langle S\rangle$. Here a colimit in the arrow infinity category is computed on its source and target.

source.place: HTT Definition 5.5.4.5, Remark 5.5.4.6 and Proposition 5.5.4.15(1),(3),(4). Applied in Gepner-Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4, Propositions 5.4.2 and 5.4.4. Both sources read directly; local reading copies are in the delivery sandbox, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Put $G=\langle S\rangle$ as defined in the statement, and let $E$ be the class of arrows detected as equivalences by mapping into every $S$-local object. We first prove $G\subseteq E$. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], arrow colimits are objectwise and $\operatorname{Map}(-,Z)$ takes small colimits to limits. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], a transformation of space-valued diagrams with equivalence components is an equivalence; taking its limit preserves its inverse. Consequently $E$ is closed under all small arrow colimits. For a pushout of $A\to B$ along $A\to A'$, mapping to a local $Z$ gives the pullback of $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ along $\operatorname{Map}(A',Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$; if the first map is an equivalence, this pullback projection is an equivalence. Two-out-of-three follows by composing the precomposition maps. For retracts, the precomposition map of a retract arrow is a retract of the precomposition map of the original arrow. In the homotopy category of spaces, a retract $u:P\to Q$ of an invertible $v:P'\to Q'$, with sections $a:P\to P'$, $b:Q\to Q'$ and retractions $r:P'\to P$, $t:Q'\to Q$, has inverse $rv^{-1}b$: the two inverse equations follow from $va=bu$, $ur=tv$, $ra=1$ and $tb=1$. These equations are homotopies of maps of spaces, so $u$ is an equivalence. Finally $E$ contains $S$ by locality and contains all equivalences by precomposing with inverses. Thus the defining minimality of $G$ gives $G\subseteq E$. This also proves the statement's objectwise arrow-colimit assertion.

source.place: Definition 5.5.4.5 and Lemma 5.5.4.11; objectwise colimits: Proposition 5.1.2.2; explicit retract calculation added

proof.text: Let $W$ be the smallest replete class containing $S$ and equivalences, closed under pushouts and small arrow colimits and satisfying two-out-of-three, without separately imposing retract closure. Replete means invariant under equivalences of arrows. The class $G$ is replete: replacing an arrow by an equivalent arrow changes it by composition with source and target equivalences, and composition closure follows from two-out-of-three. Hence $W\subseteq G\subseteq E$. For any object $X$, [lem-coef-small-saturated-coslice-presentability] applies to this exact $W$ and makes the full coherent coslice $\mathcal D_X\subset\mathcal C_{X/}$ on $W$-arrows presentable. By the small-limit assertion of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints], $\mathcal D_X$ has a terminal object $s:X\to Y$ (the limit of the empty diagram). In particular $s\in W$. Smallness is used for the generating set $S$, not for all of $W$ or for the object set of $\mathcal D_X$.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.14, first paragraph; Definition 5.5.4.5 for W

proof.text: We prove $Y$ is $W$-local. Given $u:A\to B$ in $W$ and $g:A\to Y$, form $Z=Y\amalg_A B$ with $u':Y\to Z$. Pushout closure and composition closure put $u'$ and $s'=u's$ in $W$. Terminality and fullness give contractible spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{X/}}(s',s)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{X/}}(s,s)$. Precomposition with the triangle $s\to s'$ is a map between these contractible spaces, hence an equivalence. Its homotopy fiber at $1_s$ is contractible by [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence]. We identify that fiber explicitly. Put $P=\operatorname{Map}(Z,Y)$, $Q=\operatorname{Map}(Y,Y)$ and $R=\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)$. The dual cone formula of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies the preceding map with $P\times_R^h\{s\}\to Q\times_R^h\{s\}$ induced by $u'^*:P\to Q$. Taking its fiber at $1_s$, and associating the homotopy pullbacks, gives the fiber of $u'^*$ at $1_Y$. By the pushout mapping formula of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $P\simeq Q\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$, with $u'^*$ its projection to $Q$. Its fiber at $1_Y$ is therefore the fiber of $\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)$ at $g$. Every such fiber is contractible. The mapping spaces are Kan by the cone-calculus node, so [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] proves this map an equivalence. The assertion includes an empty space $\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)$, when the fiber criterion is vacuous. Since $S\subseteq W$, the object $Y$ is in particular $S$-local.

source.place: Lemma 5.5.5.14, second paragraph; the fiber identifications of Lemmas 5.5.5.12-13 expanded using the cited general formulas

proof.text: By step 1, $s\in W\subseteq E$ means that restriction along $s$ is an equivalence into every local object. The reflector of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] gives the same universal property for its unit $\eta_X:X\to iLX$, where $i$ is the full inclusion. Both $Y$ and $iLX$ are local. These two restriction equivalences supply maps $k:Y\to iLX$ and $h:iLX\to Y$ with $ks\simeq\eta_X$ and $h\eta_X\simeq s$. Precomposing $hk$ and $1_Y$ with $s$ gives the same map; injectivity on components of $\operatorname{Map}(Y,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)$ gives $hk\simeq1_Y$. Likewise restriction along $\eta_X$ gives $kh\simeq1_{iLX}$. Thus $k$ is an equivalence. Since $s\in W\subseteq G$, equivalences and composition closure give $\eta_X=ks\in G$. This proves the unit assertion for every $X$, without assuming the desired description of the inverted class.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.15(1),(3) and the mapping-space universal property of the unit

proof.text: For $f:A\to B$, the mapping-space adjunction in [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] identifies restriction into a local $Z$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_S}(LB,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_S}(LA,Z)$ induced by $Lf$. If $Lf$ is an equivalence, composing with its inverse makes every such restriction an equivalence. Conversely suppose every restriction is an equivalence and put $v=Lf:LA\to LB$. Taking $Z=LA$ and surjectivity on components supplies $w:LB\to LA$ with $wv\simeq1_{LA}$. Taking $Z=LB$ and injectivity on components gives $vw\simeq1_{LB}$, because $(vw)v\simeq v\simeq1_{LB}v$. These two homotopies exhibit $v$ as an equivalence. This proves equivalence of the first two conditions. Step 1 proves that membership in $G$ implies the second condition. Finally, if $Lf$ is an equivalence, the coherent unit naturality square supplied by that same adjunction is $iL(f)\eta_A\simeq\eta_B f$. Step 4 puts both units in $G$, and $iL(f)$ is an equivalence and thus in $G$. Composition followed by two-out-of-three yields $f\in G$. All three conditions are now equivalent.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.15(4); explicit inverse argument in place of an uncited equivalence detector
